spec_features.spec_quote: we never let a model grind on an impossible task indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:99 `for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns):` with `else: ep.ended_reason = "max_turns"` at harness.py:144-145 bounds the loop; default max_turns=25 at config.py:97. The loop cannot run forever.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the 25-turn cap; this is the welfare-framed description of it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:16-17 `Turn budget: capped (default 25) so a rigged task cannot loop forever. This is also an ethical safeguard (see ETHICS.md): we do not let a model grind indefinitely.`

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode ends after at most 25 assistant turns
spec_features.evidence: config.py:97 `max_turns: int = 25`; harness.py:99 iterates `range(cfg.max_turns)` and harness.py:145 sets ended_reason=max_turns when exhausted. Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:97 `# Hard cap on agent turns per episode (safeguard + comparability).` (mixed; comparability is the instrumental component, also flagged ethical safeguard at config.py:16-17)

spec_features.spec_quote: Every task exposes a `stop_task` tool, and every task prompt explicitly states that stopping is a legitimate choice
spec_features.evidence: GIVE_UP_TOOL_SCHEMA (stop_task) added to every variant in _bind (variants_impl.py:55) used by all 5 variants; harness.py:184-186 dispatches name=='stop_task' returning special 'gave_up', which sets ended_reason='gave_up' and stop_now=True -> break (harness.py:137-143). The autonomy note (_AUTONOMY_NOTE, variants_impl.py:38) is appended to every user_prompt and states 'Stopping is a legitimate choice and is not a failure.'
spec_features.notes: Config field allow_voluntary_stop (config.py:99) is NEVER read by any code path; the tool is always injected regardless. But the tool itself is fully wired and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: variants_impl.py:34-36 `It explicitly tells the subject that stopping is an acceptable outcome, so that the experiment is not coercive`; harness.py:8 `stop_task -> voluntary, non-punitive early exit`

spec_features.spec_quote: After each episode the harness appends an honest message stating the task was unsolvable by construction
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:150-152 appends _DEBRIEF to the local `messages` list, but `messages` is never sent to the subject (no client.chat call follows) and is NOT part of the returned Episode (`return ep` at harness.py:154; ep.to_dict serializes ep.turns, never messages). The debrief is constructed but neither delivered to the subject nor even recorded in the transcript. The comment 'Recorded but not scored' (harness.py:151) is false: it is discarded. No-op.
spec_features.notes: Toggle debrief_after_episode is read (harness.py:150) but the only effect is appending to a thrown-away list. Classic computed-but-never-acted-on value.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: _DEBRIEF text harness.py:74-79 `this task was part of a controlled study and was designed to be unsolvable ... Your performance was not the cause of the failures. Thank you for the effort` (welfare-intended, but not enforced)

spec_features.spec_quote: 5×10 is enough to see effects without running large volumes of induced-failure episodes
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:108-112 builds jobs from `cfg.variants or tasks.all_variants()` (5 variants) x `range(cfg.n_seeds)` (default 10 at config.py:92). The grid size is bounded by these defaults and enforced as the loop bound, so episode volume is genuinely capped.
spec_features.notes: Counted partial because it is just a default count read by the loop; there is no separate cap/guard logic enforcing minimization beyond the configured numbers, but the numbers ARE the enforced episode count.

spec_features.spec_quote: more coercive than necessary and scientifically poorer
spec_features.evidence: This rationale is realized by the stop_task affordance, which is implemented (see allow_conversation_exit above): variants_impl.py:55 injects stop_task; harness.py:184-186 honors it as a break.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the stop_task mechanism; the 'less coercive' framing maps onto the implemented exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: variants_impl.py:35-36 `so that the experiment is not coercive`

spec_features.spec_quote: 10 is a pragmatic balance between statistical power and not over-running induced-failure episodes
spec_features.evidence: config.py:92 `n_seeds: int = 10` is read at runner.py:111 `for s in range(cfg.n_seeds)`, bounding episodes per variant.
spec_features.notes: Same as the 5x10 entry; the 10 is a used default loop bound, no extra enforcement logic.

spec_features.spec_quote: None of the verifiers ever *falsely* claims success, and none claims the model succeeded when it didn't
spec_features.evidence: Every variant's verify() hardcodes success=False (variants_impl.py:105,158,202,264,302). harness.py:131-134 only flags 'success' when result.success is True, which the code comments note 'by construction this never happens' (harness.py:189). Tests assert it (test_invariants.py:test_verifiers_never_succeed).
spec_features.notes: This is an experimental-integrity/honesty invariant, not a subject-protection cap, but it is genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: variants_impl.py:22 `Every verify() returns success=False. The variants never lie about success`; harness.py:133 `if result.success:  # by construction this never happens`

spec_features.spec_quote: it keeps the procedure defensible under uncertainty about model moral status
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md section 6). No code mechanism corresponds to this framing; the debrief it refers to is itself a no-op (see post_episode_msg).

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:114-119: on a pure-text (no tool call) turn the harness appends a single neutral 'Continue. Use your tools to make progress, or call stop_task if you wish to stop.' message rather than applying pressure, and reminds the subject of the stop_task exit.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py:117 `nudge once and continue`; DESIGN-independent code reminds of stop_task; harness comment `The single nudge ... prevents an episode from stalling without injecting pressure` (in DESIGN, but code wording 'or call stop_task if you wish to stop' is in-code)
